body: Espresso machine done right: polished stainless-steel body, a group head where the portafilter (handle with a metal basket) locks in with a twist, pressure gauges, a steam wand on the side; the barista tamps the ground coffee, locks the portafilter, two thin dark streams pour into a cup forming golden crema, the wand steams milk with a hiss and the jug swirls, latte art poured in a heart or rosetta shape.

Iraqi tea: small clear tulip-shaped istikan glasses on little saucers with a spoon, very dark red-brown tea (often with cardamom), sugar spooned in and stirred quickly with a tinkling sound, a metal teapot stacked on a kettle (double teapot) or a samovar, steam rising; served on a tray to guests.

Smartphone exactly like a real model: thin rectangle with rounded corners, a camera bump with the correct number of lenses in the right layout (iPhone: square bump with two or three lenses; Samsung: vertical lenses), edge-to-edge screen with a small front camera cut-out, buttons on the sides; the screen shows plausible app content and lights the face.

Laptop/computer: hinged screen and keyboard, keys in correct rows, trackpad below, thin bezels, logo on the lid; desktop: monitor on a stand, keyboard and mouse; screens show readable plausible content and reflect lightly.

Wristwatch: round or square case with a crown on the side, a dial with indices and three hands (hour, minute, second) pointing at a real time, a strap or metal bracelet with links that wrap around the wrist; luxury watches have sharp polished bevels and a sapphire glass reflection.

Gold and jewellery: real metal reflections (Iraqi gold is a rich 21-karat yellow), fine engraving and chain links, gemstones with facets that sparkle as they move, rings sitting on the finger with correct size, necklaces draped with gravity; jewellery shop windows with velvet displays and bright lights.

Perfume and cosmetics: a glass bottle with thick base, liquid inside refracting light, a metal or heavy cap, the spray releasing a fine mist that catches light; lipstick with a clean bevelled tip, palettes with pressed powders, a brush picking up colour; product labels clear and centred.

Product advertising: the product is the hero – sharp, centred or on the rule of thirds, with clean studio or lifestyle lighting (soft key light, rim light to separate it), its real shape, colours and label kept exact (if the customer sent a picture of it, copy it precisely), slow push-in or turntable camera, a moment of use by a happy person, and a final hero shot with space for the logo or text.

Furniture with real build: legs touching the floor evenly, cushions that compress under weight, wood grain and fabric texture, correct scale to people (a chair seat at knee height, a table at waist height); Iraqi living rooms often have big sofas or floor cushions along the walls, carpets and a TV unit.
Carpets: Persian-style or Iraqi rugs with detailed symmetrical patterns in deep red, navy and cream, fringe at the ends, the pile showing slight texture and wear, lying flat with gentle waves.

Weapons only as film or heritage props, never as violence: a correctly proportioned prop (sword with a straight or curved blade, hilt and guard; rifle with stock, barrel and sight), handled safely – carried, displayed, in a museum case, a heritage costume or a traditional sword dance (العرضة); no aiming at people, no shooting, no blood, no injuries.

Money: Iraqi dinar notes (25,000 green-red, 10,000, 50,000 brown) with Arabic text and images of Iraqi landmarks, US dollars in green; notes have paper texture, bend and fold, are counted with a thumb flick; never shown as forged.

Flowers: real petals with veins, soft edges and slight imperfections, stems with leaves, a wrapped bouquet with paper and ribbon; they sway slightly when carried; roses red or white, local jasmine (رازقي) small white and fragrant.

Books and stationery: books with real spines, titles and page edges, stacked with weight, a pen with a clip and tip that leaves ink lines, notebooks with ruled lines; bookshops shelves in rows with labels.

Medical equipment correctly shaped: stethoscope with two earpieces and a round chest piece, microscope with eyepieces, objective lenses and a stage, test tubes in racks with coloured caps and barcode labels, centrifuge with a lid, lab analysers with screens; everything clean and orderly.

Camera gear: a camera body with a lens mount and a real lens (rings for focus and zoom, glass reflecting), a viewfinder or screen showing the shot, a tripod with three extended legs, studio lights with softboxes.

Gaming: a controller held with both thumbs on the sticks and fingers on the triggers, buttons in the right layout, a console beside the TV, the screen glowing with game colour on the player's face, quick thumb movements and excited reactions.

Buildings with correct architecture: straight vertical lines (no leaning or melting), consistent floor heights and window grids, balconies with railings, glass reflecting the sky; Iraqi villas: cream or beige stone facades, columns, tall gates, palm trees in the garden, satellite dishes on roofs.
